The histidine triad nucleotide-binding protein 1 (HINT1) gene has been suggested as a potential candidate for schizophrenia by data from both association and expression studies. These studies have found associations between HINT1 variants and schizophrenia in some populations, but also note that high-resolution loci such as the SPEC2/PDZ-GEF2/ACSL6 locus may be involved.

However, it's essential to consider that these findings were reported previously in other samples, which can make it challenging to isolate the association signals. Additional research may be needed to distinguish between candidate genes and identify the specific genetic markers associated with schizophrenia.

Furthermore, there are concerns about the specificity of some studies examining HINT1, as some have raised questions about the reliability of the genetic associations reported. Overall, while HINT1 has been proposed as a potential candidate for schizophrenia, more research is needed to fully understand its role in this condition.
